methodology: Direct reading of production code (never inferred from prior docs alone): lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/chain.ts (computeOperativeDocument), lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/types.ts (OperativeDocumentResolution, NodeSupersessionIndex/Record/Status), lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/operative-state.ts (computeOperativeContractState, buildNodeSupersessionIndex, getNodeSupersessionStatus, resolveNodeWithSupersessionAwareness's own call site in semantic/tools.ts), lib/contract-model/analysis/orchestrator.ts (real production call sites), plus a full repo grep for every consumer of buildNodeSupersessionIndex/getNodeSupersessionStatus/NodeSupersessionStatus/CURRENT_OPERATIVE.

pathA_wholeDocumentResolution.consumer: computeOperativeContractState (operative-state.ts:506) calls it and attaches the result, unmodified, as OperativeContractState.operativeDocument
pathA_wholeDocumentResolution.storage: Not persisted separately - a pure, in-memory field of the OperativeContractState object computed once per (instrument, asOfDate) by orchestrator.ts's analyzeInstrument, held only for the duration of that analysis run.
pathA_wholeDocumentResolution.confirmed: computeOperativeDocument builds a directed graph over RESOLVED-target RESTATE_AGREEMENT effects (successor restates predecessor) and returns status RESOLVED/REVIEW_REQUIRED/NOT_APPLICABLE with operativeDocumentId + predecessorDocumentIds + relationshipChain only when status is RESOLVED. Verified this correctly returns RESOLVED with doc-c operative, predecessors [doc-a, doc-b] against the real frozen Riot evidence when all three documents' text and effects are supplied together (docs/pre-unseen-classifier-remediation/07-riot-deterministic-replay.json, produced after the classifier fix in the prior session).

pathB_nodeSupersession.readsOnly: For each {baseDocumentId, state} entry, this function iterates ONLY state.provisions (OperativeProvisionView[] - per-SECTION/per-DEFINITION amendment history) and populates supersededByNodeId from provision.supersededSourceNodeIds (a node pushed there only when a real SECTION- or DEFINITION-kind amendment effect's own applied-chain iteration overwrote it in buildProvisionView).
pathB_nodeSupersession.neverReads: state.operativeDocument is never referenced anywhere in buildNodeSupersessionIndex's own body (confirmed by direct reading of the full function, operative-state.ts lines 560-606) - the whole-document RESTATE_AGREEMENT graph result is completely invisible to this function.
pathB_nodeSupersession.consumer: getNodeSupersessionStatus(index, documentId, nodeId) (operative-state.ts:628) - a node whose documentId IS covered (an OperativeContractState was computed for it) and whose nodeId never appears in supersededByNodeId or ambiguousNodeIds defaults to CURRENT_OPERATIVE (operative-state.ts:642), regardless of whether that document itself is a resolved predecessor in a DIFFERENT document's whole-document chain.
pathB_nodeSupersession.reproduced: doc-a::6.01(d) (a real, frozen structural node - the EXCEPTION carve-out both blind ground-truth reviewers confirmed present in doc-a/doc-b, silently deleted in doc-c) reports CURRENT_OPERATIVE via this exact path even when computeOperativeContractState for doc-a's own instrument simultaneously reports operativeDocument.status=RESOLVED with doc-a itself inside predecessorDocumentIds (docs/pre-unseen-classifier-remediation/08-deleted-carveout-check.json, produced by the prior session, re-confirmed by direct code reading this session).

rootCauseConfirmation.statement: CONFIRMED, not materially different from the mission's own stated expectation: node/source currentness (buildNodeSupersessionIndex/getNodeSupersessionStatus) does not consume resolved whole-document supersession (OperativeContractState.operativeDocument) at all. The two mechanisms are structurally independent code paths that happen to both be called once per instrument by the same orchestrator, with no data flow between them. No STOP condition triggered.

consumerAccessPatternConfirmed.everyRealProductionCallSiteBuildsOneEntr: grep-confirmed: every production call site that builds a NodeSupersessionIndex (orchestrator.ts:377, semantic/tools.ts:466, semantic/compile.ts:84, semantic-verification/verify.ts:311) passes a SINGLE-element array `[{ baseDocumentId, state }]` - one OperativeContractState for exactly the instrument/document currently being analyzed. No production call site ever passes multiple entries at once.
consumerAccessPatternConfirmed.implicationForFix: Because buildNodeSupersessionIndex is always called per-instrument in production, and computeOperativeContractState's own operativeDocument field (chain.ts's computeOperativeDocument) is computed FROM THAT SAME instrument's own baseDocumentId, the fix does not need any new input threaded in - state.operativeDocument is already present on the exact OperativeContractState object buildNodeSupersessionIndex already receives. This keeps the fix a pure, local, additive read of an already-computed field - never a new detection pass, never a second version-chain algorithm (mission's explicit 'do not duplicate' requirement).

importantDisclosedRefinement_instrumentS.severity: DISCLOSED_ARCHITECTURE_LIMITATION - not a stop condition, not caused or worsened by this session, out of scope to fix here (would require package-graph/instrument-grouping redesign, explicitly excluded by this mission)
importantDisclosedRefinement_instrumentS.finding: computeOperativeDocument's own whole-document graph is built exclusively from `allEffects` supplied to computeOperativeContractState for ONE instrument's own document family. Per operative-state.ts's own header comment (line ~498-505) and confirmed by re-reading orchestrator.ts's analyzeInstrument (documents: instrumentDocs is scoped to unit.documentIds), instrument-grouping only MERGES two documents into one instrument when their restatement relationship resolved with RESOLVED confidence - a REVIEW_REQUIRED-confidence link (like Riot's doc-b->doc-c relationship, 0.7 confidence DETERMINISTIC_CHRONOLOGICAL_PREDECESSOR) never merges them into the same instrument, by design (this is unchanged, pre-existing behavior from the prior post-3F.2 remediation session, not touched here).
importantDisclosedRefinement_instrumentS.consequenceForRiot: In a REAL, per-instrument-scoped orchestrator run (not the prior session's own deterministic-replay script, which deliberately supplied all three documents' text/effects to ONE combined computeOperativeDocument/runAmendmentPipeline call to demonstrate the algorithm's own chain-closure property in isolation), doc-a+doc-b would form ONE instrument (RESOLVED merge) with its own operativeDocument resolving {operativeDocumentId: doc-b, predecessorDocumentIds: [doc-a]} - it has no visibility into doc-c at all, since doc-c's own text/effects are never supplied to this instrument's own runAmendmentPipeline call. doc-c would be a SEPARATE instrument whose own operativeDocument resolves {operativeDocumentId: doc-c, predecessorDocumentIds: [doc-b]} - again with no visibility into doc-a.
importantDisclosedRefinement_instrumentS.practicalImpactOnThisMission: This session's fix (Rule 1 below) still correctly and fully closes the mission's own governing invariant WITHIN each instrument's own resolved scope: doc-a's own instrument affirmatively knows doc-a is a resolved predecessor of doc-b, so doc-a::6.01(d) correctly stops being CURRENT_OPERATIVE inside that instrument's own supersessionIndex - the exact node/document trust inconsistency this mission targets is closed. What does NOT happen (and must not be claimed to happen) is a single node-trust computation asserting doc-a is a predecessor of doc-c across the REVIEW_REQUIRED instrument boundary - that boundary itself remains an honest, pre-existing, disclosed uncertainty (doc-b->doc-c is never guessed as RESOLVED), consistent with mission Rule 4 ('material unresolved state -> route uncertainty, never guess'). This is disclosed in full in 08-riot-deterministic-replay.json and 09-historical-node-trust-check.json rather than overclaimed.
importantDisclosedRefinement_instrumentS.verifiedNotAStopCondition: This is a refinement of WHERE the already-correct algorithm's boundaries lie (a pre-existing instrument-grouping policy decision, unrelated to node/document trust consistency), not a contradiction of the root cause above. The core defect - node supersession blind to whole-document supersession - is exactly as expected and is fully fixed within realistic per-instrument scope.

conclusion: Proceeding to implementation per mission Section 4-8 (RULE 1-4 currentness composition), integrating at buildNodeSupersessionIndex/getNodeSupersessionStatus exactly as the mission's own default-expected root cause anticipated, with the instrument-scoping nuance above disclosed transparently rather than hidden or overclaimed.
